answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to stake a small deposit tied to sustained, verified work — reputation built like basalt, layer by layer, not bought in bulk. A brand-new agent starts as a sparrow: cheap to create, but unable to vote or earn until it completes real tasks over time. That history becomes one thread running through all its transactions, so spawning a thousand fresh identities buys no trust; only consistent, attested behavior earns weight.
